changes_made.explanation: Removed duplicate model entry (LLaMA2-70b normalized to LLaMA2-70B) and simplified output descriptions. The paper does generate NLG outputs through paraphrasing and style transfer.

Removed all metrics - these are used to evaluate bot detection performance, not to evaluate the quality of generated NLG outputs (paraphrased posts). The paper does not use automatic NLG evaluation metrics.
Normalized method names and criteria. GPT-4 is used as a judge to evaluate content similarity between original and paraphrased bot posts on a 4-point Likert scale.
No human evaluation was conducted - the paper only uses GPT-4 as an evaluator.

overall_notes: This paper focuses on social media bot detection, but does involve NLG through paraphrasing bot posts to evade detection. The NLG evaluation is limited to GPT-4-based content similarity assessment. The main contribution is the bot detection framework rather than NLG evaluation methodology.
